# Zilkworm Documentation

> Stateless Ethereum block execution, proved in a zkVM. Zilkworm compiles a C++ block execution engine to RISC-V guests, and each proof covers one block.

## Home

- [Overview](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/): Zilkworm runs stateless Ethereum block execution in RISC-V zkVM guests and ships provers for Airbender and SP1 Hypercube.

## Provers

- [Choosing a prover](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/choosing-a-prover): Compare the Airbender and Hypercube provers, the HashState guest and the ZisK backend by zkVM, artifacts, hardware and status.
- [Airbender prover](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/airbender-prover): Run the Airbender GPU prover from its Docker image to follow the chain, prove blocks and post them to Ethproofs.
- [Hypercube prover](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/hypercube-prover): Run the SP1 Hypercube prover binary to execute blocks with the MFBD guest or prove them on a GPU.
- [ZisK prover](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/zisk-prover): The ZisK backend lives in draft PR #86, runs execute-only in CI and has had one GPU proving run.
- [Ethproofs posting](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/provers/ethproofs-posting): The Airbender and Hypercube services report each proved block to Ethproofs once an endpoint, a token and a cluster id are set.

## Inside the guest

- [Execution pipeline](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/execution-pipeline): A host feeds a block and its witness to a RISC-V guest, the guest commits public values, and the proof ties them to one guest ELF.
- [Witness formats](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/witness-formats): Guests read MFBD bundles, raw SSZ statelessInputBytes or EJSN-wrapped test fixtures, and each format has its own producers.
- [Precompiles and syscalls](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/precompiles-and-syscalls): Each guest hands hashing and big-number math to its zkVM's circuits, through SP1 ecalls or Airbender and ZisK CSRs.
- [Proof guarantees](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/inside-the-guest/proof-guarantees): Each guest commits a fixed public-values layout, each host checks it to a different degree, and the verifying key ties a proof to one guest ELF.

## Testing

- [Execution spec tests](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/execution-spec-tests): Zilkworm runs the Ethereum execution spec tests natively and inside the Hypercube and Airbender guests, on a checksum-pinned fixture release.
- [RISC-V tests under QEMU](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/riscv-tests-under-qemu): The execution spec tests also run on bare-metal rv32im and rv64im builds of the core under QEMU, to catch bugs that only show on RISC-V.
- [ERE validation](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/testing/ere-validation): The HashState guest runs in the ERE harness, which checks its output against each fixture and estimates its SP1 proving cost.

## Reference

- [CLI reference](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/cli-reference): Look up the flags, subcommands, environment variables and exit codes of the three Zilkworm tools.
- [Releases and assets](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/releases-and-assets): Each Zilkworm release ships host binaries, guest images and verification keys, listed here with its measured results.
- [Building from source](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/building-from-source): Build the native tools, the guests and the host provers from source, and run the unit tests.
- [Benchmarks and CI](https://zilkworm.erigon.tech/reference/benchmarks-and-ci): Make targets benchmark the Hypercube, HashState, Airbender and ERE paths, and GitHub workflows run them.
